title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Efficiency and safety of road transport along the East-West Highway (EWH) improved

Annual average number of fatalities between Chumateleti and Argveta over 5 years fell to 9.0 or fewer Progress/Status: Assessment of outcome shall be made at completion of works. Data Source: Roads Department's annual accident data statistics (sex-disaggregated) Actual value:

Average travel time between Chumateleti and Argveta reduced to 45 minutes Progress/Status: Assessment of outcome shall be made at completion of works. Data Source: Project completion report Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Overload control implemented Indicator: 38 portable scales commissioned (2019 baseline: 0 under the project) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Review of draft bidding document for the 38 portable scales was put on hold.
During the Jul 2021 Inception Mission, the Mission advised to harmonize the implementation of overload control strategy with the procurement of portable weigh scales and the 2 weigh bridges. It was agreed that the RD will complete internal consultations as to which agency will operate the weigh stations and portable weigh scales and propose a roll out plan to ADB by end 2021.
The draft bidding documents for the procurement of portable scales has been submitted informally to ADB for review and comments in Oct 2021.
ADB approved the bidding documents on 24 Feb 2022. The IFB was posted on 28 Feb 2022, with a deadline for submission of bids on 11 Apr 2022.
Bid opening was held on 11 Apr 2022 and 2 bids were received (one bid was submitted late and will be returned unopened).
ADB provided no objection to BER on 4 Jul 2022 for the procurement of 38 portable scales.
Unit Export Limited delivered the Performance Security on 10 Oct 2022. Bid validity extended until 22 Nov 2022 (3rd extension) to allow Roads Department to complete internal approval procedures.
Contract signed on 18 Nov 2022 with Unit Export Limited for the Procurement of 38 Portable Scales.
ADB approved Amendment 1 on 13 Feb 2023 and Amendment 2 on 7 Mar 2023.
All deliverables under the 38 Portable Scales contract have been completed: the supplier delivered the goods and conducted training for installation and commissioning of the goods.
The original contract completion was three months after the contract signing, which was extended for one month (revised contract completion date was 20 Mar 2023).
Data Source: Roads Department and consultant's reports

Output: Overload control implemented Indicator: At least 1 weigh-in-motion site on the EWH with 2 corresponding weigh bridges constructed Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: During October 2023 review mission, RD informed that there is an ongoing consultation with the Ministry of Internal Affairs regarding the proposed construction of 2 weigh bridges to: (i) agree on the location; and (ii) develop an MOU for its operation by the Patrolling Police. The procurement of weigh-in-motion equipment will commence in Q2 2024. RD will inform ADB of the outcome of its consultations.
During Mar 2024 review mission, the RAMS Specialist informed that construction of 2 weigh bridges (at a static location) is put on hold while discussions on the establishment of a traffic control center is ongoing. Procurement is expected to commence in Q4 2024.
During Sep/Oct 2024 review mission, it was agreed with RD that construction of 2 weigh bridges (at a static location) will be put on hold while discussions on the establishment of a traffic control center is ongoing. Decision on whether to procure the weigh stations will be communicated to ADB by Q1 2025.
During Mar 2025 review mission, RD informed that an ITS based solutions is being developed for road management, which will need integration of weigh control measures. Hence, RD considers it premature to construct weigh bridges (at a static location) and instead intends using the latest technology considering wider coverage across the national road network, to be considered for financing in future loans. Therefore, RD will request the deletion of this output from the loan.
During March 2025 review mission, RD informed that an ITS based solutions for road management is being developed, which will need integration of weigh control measures. Hence, RD considers it premature to construct weigh bridges (at a static location) and instead intends using latest technology consider wider coverage across the national road network, to be considered for financing in future Loans. RD will request the deletion of this output from the loan.
Procurement of weigh bridge component is expected to commence in Q3 2026.
Data Source: Roads Department and consultant's reports

Output: Road safety increased Indicator: At least 50% of roadside village residents increased awareness on road safety Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: During the Apr 2021 inception mission, Mission discussed the institutional development components, and it was agreed with the RD to harmonize the implementation of these components under F2 and F4 loans. RD will complete internal consultations and provide a rollout plan for ADB's review by Q3 2021.
The road safety audit will be conducted after the civil works are completed.
The project team and RD agreed during Sep 2021 Review Mission (combined with F2 MTR) that the activities for the road safety awareness component, and capacity building for operation and maintenance and project management component under Loan 3715-GEO (F2) and Loan 3861-GEO (F4) will be harmonized for implementation: (i) road safety campaigns for both F2 and F4 will be done in May 2022 and 2023 during UN Road Safety week; (ii) project management training program will be planned by Dec 2021, the training arrangements finalized by Aug 2022, and delivered by end of 2022; and (iii) the road maintenance sustainability strategy draft - currently under MRDI's review - to be shared with ADB for review and comments.
Recruitment of Road Safety and Entrepreneurship and Livelihood Development Training consultants is ongoing. ADB approved Submission 1 (CQS) for Road Safety and Entrepreneurship Consultant on 5 Jul and 11 Jul 2023, respectively.
ADB approved the Submission 2-3 (CQS) for Road Safety and Entrepreneurship Consultant on 16 Oct 2023.
Road Safety and Entrepreneurship contract with Partnership for Road Safety Foundation signed on 1 Nov 2023. The contract was completed on 31 Oct 2024.
Livelihood Development Training contract with Policy and Management Consulting Group (PMCG) signed on 31 Oct 2023. The contract was completed on 31 Aug 2024. Data Source: Supervision consultant's road safety reports
Output: Road safety increased Indicator: including 50% of women Data Source: Supervision consultant's road safety reports Actual value:

Output: Shorapani and Argveta section constructed Indicator: 1 rest stop constructed at the Zestaponi interchange with EWCD-friendly features Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: During October 2023 review mission, RD informed that the location of the rest stop has been identified (Shorapani junction area). It will be carried out through PPP.
As discussed during March 2024 review mission, RD proposed to cancel this component given the change in government priorities and will request it through the MOF.
RD proposed to change the wording "rest stop" with "market place". Based on the government's decision, instead of the F2 section (Khevi-Ubisa Section), a market space that also accommodates rest stop features will be arranged near the F4 section (Shorapani-Argveta).
ADB approved a DMF-related minor change in scope memo on 4 December 2024. Data Source: Supervision consultant's annual project progress reports

Output: Shorapani and Argveta section constructed Indicator: About 14.7 km of an access-controlled dual carriageway or 4-lane divided highway constructed to 100 km/hour design standard, partly on new alignment (RFI A) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Civil works contract for Shorapani-Argveta F4 section was signed on 16 Jan 2020 (JV Guizhou Highway Engineering Group Co. Ltd. and China National Technical Import&Export Corporation, PRC). Mobilization works are ongoing.
ADB approved the Amendment 1 to F4 works contract on 7 Apr 2020 replacing the CNY portion of the ACA to GEL.
Construction supervision consultant's contract for F4 section was signed on 11 May 2020 (JV UBM and SMEC).
In spite of COVID-19 pandemic, mobilization works has started.
The construction supervision consultant mobilized on 15 Oct 2020.
The notice to commence work was issued to contractor on 20 Oct 2020.
LARP implementation is almost 98% complete with 5 land plots under ongoing expropriation.
Compliance Report No. 3 (CR3) for Segments 13-14 approved by ADB on 26 January 2022. CR3 is the last one as per the original LARP and Addendum. However, new LAR impacts are expected due to re-design of Tunnel 6 (from closed to open cut), and hence there will be further CR(s) for the LARP Addendum (expected to be received from GEO RD in early February).
Contractor's efforts visible to increase the pace of works and catch-up. Arrangements made for steel plates, and for tunnel excavation by road headers.
Midterm Review mission fielded from 26 Sep to 10 Oct 2022 to review the implementation of the progress of the project.
As of 30 Mar 2023, estimated progress of executed works for the Shorapani-Argveta Section (F4) is about 47% in 81% time elapsed. Works are ongoing on bridges, tunnels, and highway.
During March/April 2023 review mission, the contractor indicated that due to some challenges encountered (i.e., geological conditions, etc.), about 8 months extension is needed to complete the works, by May 2024. A new work program will be submitted by the Contractor.
ADB approved on 27 Apr 2023 the Addendum to CR4 (prepared for the design changes of Tunnel 6).
The Roads Department and the Contractor have agreed on a sectional completion, whereby 9 kms are planned to be completed and opened to traffic in January 2024, and first 6 kms in June 2024.
ADB approved on 14 Dec 2023 the extension of the time for completion of works up to and including 30 June 2024, including agreements on other related terms between the RD and the Contractor (Amendment No. 3).
Cumulative physical progress as of end March 2024 for F4 section is approx. 82%. A sectional completion, whereby the later 9 kms will be completed and opened to traffic by end April 2024, and first 5 kms in June 2024.
Contractor has not signed the Amendment 3 (extension until 30 June 2024) and a further extension of the completion of the works contract is being discussed.
The Shorapani-Argveta Section (F4) was completed and inaugurated by the Prime Minister of Georgia and opened to traffic on 22 October 2024 --- 9 kms were substantially completed, inaugurated, and opened to traffic on 26 April 2024, and the remaining 5 kms on 22 October 2024.
ADB approved a DMF-related minor change in project scope on 4 Dec 2024 to: (i) cancel the secondary roads and performance-based maintenance components from the loan; (ii) cancel the road safety works on nearby sections of EWH; and (iii) shift the Road Maintenance Strategy component currently under L3715-GEO to L3861-GEO.
Contractor has substantially completed the works, and road is now open to public. DNP will continue till 22 Oct 2026.
Data Source: Supervision consultant's annual project progress reports

Output: Shorapani and Argveta section constructed Indicator: and with 5 of 10 commercial stalls allocated to female entrepreneurs Data Source: Supervision consultant's annual project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Capacity of RD for operation and maintenance improved Indicator: Road maintenance sustainability strategy, with gender-inclusive provisions, accepted by the MRDI (2017 baseline: no strategy exists) Progress/Status: Due to time constraints related to the completion of Loan 3715-GEO (31 Dec 2024), the development of the Road Maintenance Sustainability Strategy was moved to Loan 3861-GEO following ADB's approval of DMF-related minor change in scope memo on 4 Dec 2024.
The draft terms of reference and cost estimate for the “Development of Road Maintenance Strategy and Road Maintenance Guideline for Strengthening Road Maintenance Practices in Georgia” is currently under ADB's review.
The revised draft TOR and cost estimate, incorporating ADB's comments, for the “Development of Road Maintenance Strategy and Road Maintenance Guideline for Strengthening Road Maintenance Practices in Georgia”, was submitted by Roads Department on 21 July 2025 for ADB's review.
The consultancy selection for "Development of Road Maintenance Strategy and Road Maintenance Guideline for Strengthening Road Maintenance Practices in Georgia” (SARP/CS/QCBS-02) was advertised in CSRN on 16 Aug 2025, with the deadline on 15 Sep 2025. Roads Department is currently evaluating the EOIs received.
